title: Linear A parser-boundary canary audit: *900 survivor, punctuation identity reveal, and corrective replay trigger
scope: JANUS Linear A blind Anchor Bench execution

raw_v0_6_observation.deduplication_reason: The word-hash and suffix-hash survivors both reveal to the same raw corpus label *900 and therefore are two representations of one underlying object, not two independent discoveries.

*902.note: distinct corpus ASCII alias for the same Unicode glyph

*904.reason: Frozen corpus mapping returns to a Linear A sign rather than Aegean punctuation.

post_score_identity_audit.authoritative_unicode_classification: U+10100, U+10101, and U+10102 are encoded in the Aegean punctuation range; U+10100 and U+10101 are explicit word separators and U+10102 is an Aegean check mark.
post_score_identity_audit.scientific_interpretation: The v0.6 effect is real as a structural regularity but does not identify a lexical, logographic, morphological, or grammatical Linear A element. A separator/check-mark family is expected to exhibit boundary-position behavior.

details: The base parser treated *900 as an ordinary non-numeric T token.
The record-role parser therefore allowed punctuation to receive word/suffix hashes and structural roles.
The same punctuation family could also participate in earlier candidate and null universes even when it was not the winning candidate.
A local v0.6-only exclusion would therefore be insufficient for a clean inferential repair.

corrective_action.policy: Remove *900, *901, *902, *903 before hashing, candidate construction, numeric adjacency, null generation, and record-role geometry; retain *904.
corrective_action.history_policy: Do not overwrite or delete pre-filter receipts. Preserve them as historical evidence and supersede them only for post-correction inference.

infrastructure_success: Blind structural scoring detected a strong and cross-region reproducible positional regularity.
Post-score identity reveal prevented the statistical regularity from being mislabeled as a new linguistic discovery.
Representation-level falsification correctly converted a would-be positive result into a parser-boundary canary.
The failure generated a stronger parser policy and a mandatory full replay instead of threshold relaxation.
scientific_success: A robust non-linguistic explanation was found for the v0.6 survivor.
The protocol rejected promotion despite very small p-values because identity semantics invalidated the candidate class.
scientific_non_success: No new Linear A anchor was established.
The apparent two-survivor count does not represent two independent discoveries.

connection_candidate.name: REPRESENTATION_BOUNDARY_CAN_MASQUERADE_AS_STRUCTURAL_ROLE
connection_candidate.statement: When formatting or punctuation markers are admitted into the same identity space as semantic tokens, a valid structural learner can produce highly replicable but non-semantic role discoveries.
connection_candidate.falsification_requirement: Generalize only after analogous boundary-marker leakage is reproduced or independently demonstrated in at least one additional domain.

Write a new canonical Linear A research-state JSON in data/

roadmap.gate: survivor passes corrected null + cross-region replication
